claims.text: A combined ESD deposition and PLD densification process will improve the surface physical and mechanical properties of components in aggressive environments.
ESD-deposited HEA coatings can exhibit good adhesion.
The substrate-adjacent region of an ESD-deposited HEA coating can be homogeneous and substantially free of pores.
The upper region of an ESD-deposited HEA coating can contain splats and micropores.
PLD post-treatment after ESD will densify the HEA coating and eliminate microporosity.
The combined treatment will remain effective during high-temperature exposure, corrosion in salt solutions, and mechanical wear.
PLD treatment will produce a denser microstructure across the coating, particularly in upper splat regions.
The kinetic energy and process control associated with PLD promote localized remelting and consolidation of an ESD-deposited HEA coating.
Localized remelting and consolidation will fill micropores in the HEA coating.
PLD densification will not compromise the adhesion supplied by ESD.
Filling micropores will enhance coating mechanical integrity and resistance to wear and corrosion.
ESD plus PLD coatings will have lower porosity than ESD-only coatings.
ESD plus PLD coatings will have higher microhardness than ESD-only coatings.
ESD plus PLD coatings will retain better adhesion under mechanical stress than ESD-only coatings.
ESD plus PLD coatings will have better wear resistance than ESD-only coatings.
ESD plus PLD coatings will have better corrosion resistance than ESD-only coatings.
Standard ESD coatings have less optimized mechanical properties than the proposed combined-treatment coatings.
The effectiveness of PLD densification depends on the initial coating quality and the selected processing parameters.
Chemical or thermal conditions beyond the tested range may compromise coating performance.
